system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of the Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on nearly every major term. Several departures are structural. Together, the 20% cap, the "all limitations apply to all Claims" rule, the universal non-reliance clause, the folding of title into the general regime, whole-data-room disclosure and the blanket buyer-knowledge bar would leave us with very little effective recourse. We should reject the package as a whole and send a mark-up built on our starting positions.

**Approvals:**
- The Seller's 20% cap and 18-month period are both conditional fallbacks in our playbook. Each needs prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft.
- No such authority has been given. We must not accept either, or signal that we might, at this stage.
- We should also confirm the 22 September 2026 data-room cut-off. That is about six weeks before today, so the facts disclosed may be out of date.

---

## 1. Liability regime

### 1.1 General cap (cl 12.1): Seller 20% / AUD 4.8m vs our 25% / AUD 6.0m
- **Departure:** The Seller has opened at our fallback figure.
- **Authority:** Accepting it requires Amelia Frost's prior written authority for this draft. None has been given.
- **Response:** Restate 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not describe 20% as a possible landing point in correspondence.

### 1.2 Thresholds (cl 12.2): de minimis AUD 25k and basket AUD 250k (excess only) vs our AUD 5k and AUD 50k (first dollar)
- **Departure:** The de minimis is five times ours and the basket is five times ours.
- **Excess-only recovery:** The switch from "first dollar" to "excess only" means AUD 250,000 of loss is permanently unrecoverable, even after the basket is exceeded.
- **Effect:** A AUD 25,000 de minimis would also screen out many genuine individual warranty losses in a business of this size.
- **Response:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.

### 1.3 Claims period (cl 12.3/13): 18 months vs our 24 months
- **Departure:** 18 months is our fallback and requires Amelia Frost's written approval. None has been given.
- **Response:** Restate 24 months after Completion.

### 1.4 "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"
This is the most dangerous drafting point in the update and should be resisted strongly.
- **Effect:** It is a hidden general-regime override. The general cap, thresholds and 18-month limit would apply by default to:
  - title and capacity claims;
  - tax and IP claims;
  - specific indemnities (Ironquay, and any we add);
  - covenant and payment claims, such as leakage, debt and funds-flow adjustments.
- **Response:** Delete it. Draft each category (Title, Tax, IP, payment, covenant, specific indemnity) with its own regime. General limitations should apply only to the claims expressly listed.

### 1.5 Fundamental / Title warranties brought into the general regime
- **Departure:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a justification. Title and capacity go to whether we receive the asset at all. Under the Seller's draft, a defect in title to the shares would be capped at AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m price and time-barred after 18 months.
- **Response:**
  - a separate Fundamental regime with a 100% cap (AUD 24m);
  - a claims period of at least six years;
  - outside the de minimis, basket and buyer-knowledge bar.

### 1.6 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)
- **Problem:** No fraud carve-out is stated.
- **Response:** Carve fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct out of all caps, baskets, de minimis, time limits, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Status:** This is a non-negotiable playbook position. Nobody on our side may waive it.
- **Enforceability:** Under NSW law, contractual exclusion of liability for one's own fraud is generally ineffective in any event. Statutory misleading-conduct protections under the ACL/Corporations Act may also not be fully excludable. We should still draft the carve-out expressly rather than rely on the general law.

---

## 2. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

### 2.1 General disclosure (Disclosure Letter §1.1–1.2; Schedule 7)
The Seller is attempting to disclose:
- everything in the data room as at 22 September 2026;
- the Accounts;
- the statutory registers;
- all publicly searchable records.

Combined with §1.4 (no admission of materiality, consent requirements and so on), this would let the Seller argue that almost any breach was disclosed. That would neutralise the warranties.

**Response:**
- Strike §1.1 and §1.2.
- Disclosure must be specific and fair: identified against particular warranties, with enough detail for us to assess the nature and scope of the matter.
- Reject any "deemed disclosure" from prudent search or public registers.
- §1.4 is acceptable as a non-admission clause. It must not be read as qualifying the warranties beyond what is specifically disclosed.

### 2.2 Buyer knowledge exclusion (cl 8.3)
- **Problem:** The clause covers the knowledge of the Buyer *and its advisers*, and anything *discoverable* from the data room or public records. It is a blanket knowledge bar plus constructive knowledge. It would effectively penalise us for doing due diligence.
- **Response:** Delete cl 8.3.
- **If a qualifier is unavoidable,** it should apply only to Seller-knowledge-qualified warranties, defined by:
  - named Seller knowledge persons;
  - after reasonable enquiry.
- **Never excused by knowledge:** title, capacity, fraud, or any specific indemnity. This matters especially here, because we *know* about Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, the bonuses and DD-006 from diligence, and these are exactly the matters we need protection on.

---

## 3. Transaction-specific issues

### 3.1 Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3; DL §2)
- **Size:** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (around 30%). DD-002 cl 11.2 is a change-control consent, with conditions in cl 11.3.
- **Seller's offer:** Reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
- **Problem:** A consent that is delivered but subject to unmet cl 11.3 conditions may not be effective. We could complete and still face termination or renegotiation rights over 30% of revenue. The Seller confirms that no final consent or evidence of satisfied conditions has been provided.
- **Response:**
  - a Condition Precedent requiring an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent;
  - documentary evidence before Completion that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied;
  - Buyer approval of the form of consent;
  - a stronger Seller obligation than reasonable endeavours alone. At minimum: all reasonable endeavours, prompt engagement, Buyer participation in discussions, and a long-stop date with a Buyer walk right.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility (cl 2/7; DL §3)
- **Status:** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding. DD-003 contains a change-control clause (8.1) and a discharge provision (9.2). The facility has not been repaid and no discharge has been provided.
- **Problem:** The Seller offers a release "following Completion". On a debt-free/cash-free deal, that risks us paying full value while the security remains over the Company's assets and change-of-control rights remain live.
- **Response:**
  - a current payout letter from Riverlark;
  - repayment made directly to Riverlark from Completion funds;
  - executed security releases and discharges, including PPSR, delivered at Completion;
  - the outstanding amount treated as Debt in the price mechanics.
- **Fallback:** A post-completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark *and* Amelia Frost's approval. Neither is in place.

### 3.3 DD-005 employee bonuses: AUD 420,000 (Funds flow; DL §5)
- **Problem:** The Seller states that the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" but are not itemised in the funds flow. The Disclosure Letter confirms this and is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs. Because the bonuses are triggered by Completion and payable by the Company, the cost would in practice fall on the Company, and therefore on us, unless it is captured.
- **Response:** Either:
  - include the AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item, treated as Debt or a transaction expense deducted from price; or
  - require them to be Seller-funded,
  
  in each case backed by a specific indemnity.
- **Supporting requests:** A statement of which employees are entitled, the conditions attached, and the tax and superannuation treatment.

### 3.4 Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL §4)
- **Background:** DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open.
- **Verification:** That figure has not been independently verified in either direction. We should not assume it is correct, unpaid or the full exposure.
- **Problem:** An indemnity limited to "the specific SOW3 payment" does not cover:
  - loss from the Company not owning or being unable to use the SOW3 materials;
  - third-party claims;
  - remediation or re-development costs;
  - any other amounts Ironquay claims.
- **Response:**
  - broaden the indemnity to all loss arising from the Ironquay/SOW3 IP position;
  - keep a cure mechanism: payment of the outstanding SOW3 fees plus a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay, ideally as a pre-Completion deliverable;
  - keep the indemnity outside the general cap, basket and knowledge bar;
  - ask for bank evidence of the payment status.

### 3.5 DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DL §6)
- **Facts disclosed:** A download link was sent to an unintended external address. The export may contain about 1,240 records. Access, scope and notification obligations have not been established.
- **Seller's position:** It calls the matter "not expected to be material". That is an assertion, not a disclosed fact.
- **Our position:** We should equally not assume there was a breach, harm, a notifiable data breach obligation, or any loss figure.
- **Response:** Covenants requiring the Seller and Company to:
  - preserve all logs and evidence;
  - complete a proper investigation, including an assessment under the Privacy Act notifiable data breaches scheme within the statutory timeframe;
  - give the Buyer regular written updates and access;
  - take no regulatory or customer communications without Buyer consultation.
- **Protection:** We should seek specific protection, such as a specific indemnity or a reserved claim, sized once the facts are known. The investigation was already "preliminary" as at 22 September, so request an update now.

### 3.6 Sandbar renewals: AUD 330,000 (DL §8)
- **Facts:** There are three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each (DD-008/DD-011), and the Seller says they should be read together.
- **Seller's position:** It calls them "ordinary-course operating costs". The Disclosure Letter itself says it does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Our position:** We should not automatically treat them as Debt or deduct them from price either.
- **Response:**
  - diligence the timing, terms, termination rights and accrual status of each renewal;
  - add a warranty on the renewals and a pre-Completion conduct restriction on further renewals without Buyer consent;
  - decide the price treatment once those facts are known.

### 3.7 Title (DL §10)
- **Problem:** The Seller relies on the DD-012 share register. That is an internal Company record supplied by the Seller, not independent proof.
- **Response:** Require independent evidence:
  - ASIC company extract;
  - original share certificates;
  - an allotment and transfer history reconciled to the register;
  - PPSR and encumbrance searches;
  - Seller board and shareholder authority for the sale;
  - confirmation that no options, convertibles or rights exist over the shares.
- **Protection:** Title warranties sit within the Fundamental regime (see 1.5).

### 3.8 Tax and IP warranties
- **Problem:** The Seller asserts these are "settled under the general regime". They are not: they remain open.
- **Response:**
  - confirm in writing that tax and IP terms are still under negotiation;
  - resist any implication that the general cap, basket and time limit apply to them;
  - negotiate separate regimes. For tax, that typically means a tax indemnity with a period tied to the amendment and limitation periods.
- **Our own position:** Equally, we should not assume we will get unlimited liability on these. They are simply open.

### 3.9 Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- **Status:** These are lower priority. The disclosures suggest a notification obligation (lease) and an anti-assignment clause (Mossvale), and neither expressly requires consent to a share sale.
- **Response:** Our counsel should confirm this independently, for example by checking for deemed-assignment or change-of-control definitions. If the lease notice is needed, make it a Completion deliverable.

---

## 4. Other points
- **Bring-down:** The Disclosure Letter is dated as at 22 September 2026. Require an updated letter, with no right for the Seller to update disclosure against the warranties between signing and Completion unless we have a walk right. Warranties should be repeated at Completion.
- **Seller's framing:** The covering note calls the package "fair and balanced". That is advocacy, and the package is not balanced relative to our baseline.

---

## 5. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | **25% / AUD 6.0m.** 20% needs Amelia Frost's written authority (none given) |
| 2 | Thresholds | AUD 25k / AUD 250k, excess only | **AUD 5k / AUD 50k, first dollar** |
| 3 | Claims period | 18 months | **24 months.** 18 needs Amelia Frost's approval (none given) |
| 4 | Limitations apply to all Claims | Default override | **Delete.** Separate regimes for Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant claims |
| 5 | Title/capacity | General regime | **100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket and knowledge bar** |
| 6 | Fraud | Not carved out | **Full carve-out from all limitations and non-reliance. Non-waivable** |
| 7 | Disclosure | Whole data room and public records | **Specific fair disclosure only** |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket, including advisers and discoverable matters | **Delete.** Any qualifier uses named persons and reasonable enquiry; never title, fraud or indemnities |
| 9 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours, consent on delivery | **Effective consent CP plus evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are met; stronger obligation** |
| 10 | Riverlark | Release after Completion | **Payout letter, direct repayment, releases at Completion.** Post-Completion only with an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost's approval |
| 11 | Bonuses | Excluded from funds flow | **AUD 420k plus on-costs itemised or Seller-funded, with indemnity** |
| 12 | Ironquay | Narrow SOW3 payment indemnity | **Broaden, keep the cure (payment plus confirmatory assignment), verify the AUD 180k** |
| 13 | DD-006 | "Not material" | **Preserve evidence, investigate, give updates; specific protection. No assumed breach or figures** |
| 14 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | **Diligence first; no automatic Debt treatment or deduction** |
| 15 | Title evidence | DD-012 register | **Independent ASIC, PPSR, certificate and authority evidence** |
| 16 | Tax/IP | "Settled" | **Confirm OPEN; separate regimes** |
| 17 | Stale disclosure | As at 22 Sep 2026 | **Updated letter; bring-down at Completion** |

**Next steps:**
1. Issue the mark-up on our starting positions.
2. Send document requests (Bluefen consent and cl 11.3 evidence, Riverlark payout letter, Ironquay bank evidence, DD-006 investigation update, bonus on-cost breakdown, independent title evidence).
3. Brief Amelia Frost on the cap and time-limit gap, so that any later use of the fallbacks is a deliberate, documented decision rather than a concession made at the table.
=== END ADVICE ===
